subject.title: Feature Request: Plugin Circuit Breaker for graceful degradation

question: Should OpenClaw add a core framework-level plugin circuit breaker, and if so what default fail modes and storage/operator surfaces are acceptable for existing plugins?
rationale: Current code only has hook timeouts and a plugin-local Active Memory breaker; the requested shared breaker would change plugin API expectations, config/default behavior, runtime storage, status output, and operator controls.

options.title: Design core breaker first
options.body: Keep this issue open for a maintainer-led design that defines generic hook attribution, SQLite-backed state, status/reset commands, and compatibility-safe default behavior before implementation.

options.title: Keep plugin-owned only
options.body: Defer a framework breaker and ask each high-risk plugin to implement its own degradation policy through existing hook/config surfaces.

options.title: Start passive telemetry only
options.body: Implement non-quarantining hook timing and failure counters first, then decide active open/half-open behavior after real deployment data.

recommendation.title: Design core breaker first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for a maintainer-led design that defines generic hook attribution, SQLite-backed state, status/reset commands, and compatibility-safe default behavior before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The current hook runner, plugin registry, and gateway runtime surfaces all point to this recent area contributor in local history.
